identification: Set of five Victorian-style spindle-back saddle-seat kitchen chairs, seats look like elm or ash (grain in photos 4 and 8 reads as elm/ash, not clearly blackwood), ring-turned spindles, legs and H-stretchers. Peddle attribution is catalogue-only, no stamp seen. Common English/colonial kitchen chair pattern; only a proven Tasmanian blackwood Peddle set would be special.

entries.note: Set of 5 blackwood George Peddle railway chairs plus a single Peddle chair, hammer. Paid locally (Gowans): shows what we might pay, not a resale price. Database record only, page not opened. Blackwood and 'railway' pattern may differ from this lot's spindle-back.

Set of six early Australian spade-back dining chairs, cedar and blackwood, Tasmanian origin, c1840. Hammer, no premium. Much earlier and finer than this lot, upper bound only. Database record only, page not opened.
Rare set of four Tasmanian blackwood dining chairs attributed to James Lumsden, c1845. Hammer. Database record only, page not opened.

viewing_check: Look under seats and on back rails for a George Peddle stamp or label; check timber (blackwood vs elm/ash) on seat undersides and legs; check for splits, repairs and whether all five are truly matching; photograph any stamp.
